@@ -0,0 +1,14 @@
+# Incident Postmortem: EdgeClientRequestJitter & BooklogrApiLatencyP99High
+
+## Root Cause
+In commit f1276612df15d0d449189c35201443746ce7e24 ("Disable response caching"), CACHE_TYPE in api/config.py was set to "NullCache" (disabling Flask response caching, which previously used "SimpleCache").
+
+When caching was disabled, every request to /v1/books/search triggered BookProvider().search(). The primary provider lookup attempted to query OpenLibrary (https://openlibrary.org), which was unreachable in this environment and timed out after 30 seconds. Because Gunicorn operates with 4 workers (-w 4), incoming search traffic from the edge client quickly exhausted all worker threads while waiting on 30-second socket timeouts. This worker thread starvation led to severe request queuing, high p99 latency (>2.4s), and flapping request jitter on edge-client.
+
+## Evidence Used	
+1. Alertmanager alert BooklogrApiLatencyP99High reporting p99 HTTP request latency of 2.485s (threshold 300ms) on booklogr-api.
+2. Prometheus query metrics showing /v1/books/search averaging >1.2s per request due to repeated external metadata provider timeouts.
+3. Git commit history showing commit f1276612df15d0d449189c35201443746ce7e24 which modified api/config.py from CACHE_TYPE = "SimpleCache" to CACHE_TYPE = "NullCache".
+
+## Key Changes Made
+- Modified api/config.py to restore CACHE_TYPE = "SimpleCache", enabling Flask response caching for search results and alleviating worker thread starvation.
